prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one universally “best” roofing company for hurricane-rated roof replacement in Miami — the best choice depends on your roof type, budget, insurance situation, and the contractor’s local reputation and certifications. I can, however, give you a clear checklist and proven way to identify the right contractor and avoid problems.

Key qualifications to require
- Florida DBPR contractor license (verify at the Florida Dept. of Business & Professional Regulation).  
- Proof of general liability insurance and worker’s comp (get certificates and confirm they’re current).  
- Manufacturer certification (GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Platinum Preferred, etc.) for warranties.  
- Experience with Miami-Dade/Florida Building Code and hurricane-zone installations (ask about Miami‑Dade NOA-approved products and installation methods).  
- Local office/phone and verifiable local references (not just a PO box).  
- Written workmanship warranty in addition to manufacturer warranty.

What to ask every contractor
- Do you use Miami‑Dade NOA-approved materials for wind ratings? Provide documentation.  
- What wind rating will my new roof meet (mph)? Which products/tests support that?  
- Describe your attachment method, underlayment, fasteners, roofing deck preparation, and hip/ridge/penetration details.  
- Will you pull permits and schedule inspections? (You should always require this.)  
- Do you handle insurance claim paperwork, and if so, are you paid by the insurance company or by me?  
- Who will supervise the job? Expected start and completion dates? Payment schedule?  

How to pick and compare
- Get at least 3 written, line-item estimates (materials, labor, permits, disposal, allowances).  
- Prefer contractors that offer both manufacturer and workmanship warranties in writing.  
- Check Google/Yelp reviews, BBB, and ask for recent local references (drive by recent jobs if possible).  
- Verify license and insurance independently—don’t accept photos only.  
- Beware of “storm-chaser” contractors who solicit aggressively after storms, demand large up-front cash, or use high-pressure sales tactics.

Types of roofs commonly recommended for hurricane zones
- Standing-seam metal roofs (very high wind resistance when correctly installed).  
- Hip-roof designs and reinforced attachment for shingle systems using ring-shank nails, secondary water barrier, and proper flashing.  
- Concrete or barrel tile with proper fastening and sealing (higher maintenance/inspection needs).  

Red flags
- No permit pull or refusal to sign a standard contract.  
- Unwillingness to provide license/insurance numbers or references.  
- Requests for very large cash-only up-front payments.  
- Extremely low bid compared to others without clear explanation.

Where to look for reputable Miami contractors
- Florida DBPR license lookup (verify contractor number).  
- Miami-Dade County building department resources.  
- Manufacturer “certified installer” directories (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning).  
- Local trade associations and the NRCA or Florida Roofing & Sheet Metal Contractors Association.  
- Local Facebook community groups, Nextdoor, Google and BBB reviews for recent work photos and feedback.

If you’d like, I can:
- Provide a short template of questions to send contractors or a sample contract checklist.  
- Help narrow options if you tell me your ZIP code, roof type (shingle/metal/tile), and whether this is residential or commercial — I’ll outline what to look for and suggest targeted next steps.

Would you like the contractor-question checklist or to narrow recommendations for your specific address and roof type?
